recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If a future work group wants every concrete relevantHistory/eventHistory element to target only the profile rather than preserving base Provenance references with SHOULD-level profile guidance, that should be handled as a separate conformance decision.
issue_request: FHIR-48829 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for the FHIR-core profile list. It asked whether ProvenanceRelevantHistory should move out of core; the accepted resolution was to retain it after Request/Event relevantHistory references were updated to point specifically to the profile.
initial_application: The issue was applied upstream by commit 88c811462a204b33b86bbf1cf5d994b3dd3c0bab, which changed the active Request and Event pattern spreadsheets from Reference(Provenance) to Reference(Provenance{http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/provenance-relevant-history}) and added mapping exceptions for concrete resources whose relevantHistory/eventHistory elements still expose Reference(Provenance).
additional_context: The FMG Zulip profile-review thread records this as part of the core-profile governance review and includes John Moehrke's clarification that ProvenanceRelevantHistory supports the FHIR-I Request pattern rather than Security ownership. FHIR-I minutes on 2025-03-10 record the Persuasive with Modification vote. source/fhir.ini actively includes request, event, provenance, and the relevant concrete resources; the profile and its core IG remain under source/provenance. Later Provenance work such as FHIR-53917 updated removal semantics in the same profile but did not reverse the retained-core or profile-reference decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no current source edit is needed. The current source already reflects the applied decision by retaining the profile in core and by using the profile-specific canonical reference in the Request and Event pattern sources that drive relevantHistory guidance.
